newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends down after May expiration.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends down after May expiration.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended lower after ranging on both sides of previous levels following the action in the expiring May contract and evening up ahead of Friday's housing starts report, traders said.
Lumber closed $1.50 per tbf lower to unchanged with July off most at $391.80 and September off $0.80 at $381.70 per tbf.
May expired earlier at $387.00, down $1.30, after trading in a $9.70 range.
Overall pressure in the market came from the continued weak undertone to cash markets. Cash trade remained quiet and this is weighing on prices, traders said.

Trading activity in futures was also subdued at times as the market awaited Friday's U.S. housing starts report. The report is expected to show a small decline in April starts compared to the previous month, they added.
The National Association of Home Builders reported a drop in its Housing Market Index for May, citing concern by builders over a slowing market and possibly higher interest rates.
